# Paper 10: LoRA (2021)

*LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models* · Module 4 — Scaling, adaptation and alignment · [Track on the site](https://arubad.github.io/AI_Research_Journey/#paper-10)

## Paper and resources
- [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685)
- [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.09685.pdf)

## Walkthrough videos
- ▶ [Umar Jamil LoRA Math & Code](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PXWYUTMt-AU)
- ▶ [AI Coffee Break LoRA Ablations](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KEv-F5UkhxU)

## Study approach
Intrinsic rank (Li et al. 2018). Section 4: freeze $W_0$, inject $\Delta W = (\alpha/r)BA$, $B = 0$ and $A \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$; Tables 5–6: adapting $W_q$ and $W_v$ at r=4 beats $W_q$ alone at r=64.

## Interview hooks
**Rapid-fire:** which layers to adapt (q, v vs all linear); when LoRA loses to full fine-tuning; [QLoRA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314) (NF4 base + bf16 adapters, double quantization); adapters, prefix tuning, IA³. SVD from Phase 1 is the math.

## Break-it experiments
1. **HAND** — 15-line `nn.Linear` wrapper. Init both A and B to zero (gradients identically zero, a saddle) or both Gaussian (ΔW ≠ 0 at step 0, corrupting the base).
   - Code: `experiments/exp1_15_line_wrapper_init_both_a_and.ipynb`
2. **HAND→AGENT** — Rank sweep r ∈ {1, 4, 64}; plot singular values of ΔW.
   - Code: `experiments/exp2_rank_sweep_r_1_4_64_plot_singula.ipynb`
